candidates.attacker_control: A user who can influence files in a built project's workspace controls the content parsed by CcmParser. For freestyle jobs, the publisher selects files by the configured include pattern; the source default is **/*.cs, so a contributor could commit an XML document named with a .cs extension, and deployments that configure the documented **/ccm.xml pattern expose that report directly. For Maven jobs, target/ccm.xml is generated from the project build.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: setValidating(false) only disables validation; it is not a secure-processing or external-entity restriction. Searches found no setFeature, secure-processing, EntityResolver, or DOCTYPE prohibition anywhere in the repository. The parser is invoked on build artifacts rather than a direct unauthenticated HTTP request, so report influence and a build trigger are required. The default pattern in CcmPublisher is inconsistent with the help text (**/ccm.xml), but this affects reachability rather than removing the parser flaw.
candidates.impact: Depending on the parser implementation and node placement, a crafted report can make the Jenkins build process fetch attacker-chosen external resources (SSRF from the agent/controller), expand external entities to disclose local files, or consume resources through entity expansion. File content can also become Metric fields such as file, unit, or classification and may subsequently be exposed through CCM warning data; that downstream exposure was not verifiable in this snapshot.
candidates.prerequisites: The CCM publisher or Maven reporter must run for a build whose report content is attacker-influenced. The effective commons-digester and SAX/JAXP implementation must permit external entity resolution, as the unhardened stack used by this Java 7-era plugin normally does; the code does not enforce any restriction. Controller-local file disclosure additionally requires the referenced file to be readable by the build process on the node running the parse.
candidates.root_cause: CcmParser creates a Commons Digester and calls digester.parse(ccmXmlFile) after only setting validation off. It never disables DOCTYPE declarations, disables external general or parameter entities, enables secure processing, sets access-external restrictions, or installs a restrictive EntityResolver. Report XML from the build workspace/target is therefore parsed with the SAX/JAXP defaults.
candidates.title: XML external entity processing in CCM report parser
candidates.trace: CcmPublisher.perform builds a FilesParser with new CcmParser(...), selects workspace files, and calls workspace.act(...); CcmReporter.perform does the same against target/ccm.xml. FilesParser passes each matched InputStream to CcmParser.parse, which calls parseCCMXmlFile. There, new Digester() is configured only with setValidating(false), setClassLoader, and fixed object/bean rules before digester.parse(ccmXmlFile). Because validation is toggled but DOCTYPE/entity processing is not, an untrusted report can cause external entity resolution before the parsed values are converted into Metric/Bug annotations.
candidates.unverified: The exact transitive commons-digester and SAX/JAXP versions/defaults are not in this source snapshot, and no parser execution or exploit payload was run. FilesParser is an external dependency, and the analysis-core rendering path that might expose entity-derived Metric fields is unavailable. Remote-agent versus controller execution and whether parse failures or error messages reveal entity content also remain unverified.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

coverage_summary: Reviewed all 51 files visible under the source scope: 24 Java sources, pom.xml, README, .gitignore, site.xml, 2 resource files, and 21 webapp help pages. Traced the CcmPublisher and CcmReporter entry points into CcmParser and Commons Digester. The P1 relation index reports 51/51 files indexed, 151 symbols, 180 calls, and 165 edges; it contains no test facts and does not resolve dependency behavior, so source text was checked for every candidate edge used. No build, tests, scanners, or runtime parser execution were performed.
limitations: Static source review only; the candidate was not runtime-confirmed.
Apache Commons Digester, FilesParser, analysis-core, and the deployed SAX/JAXP implementation are external dependencies not included in the snapshot; their exact versions and defaults are unverified.

The P1 relation index is navigational and syntactic, not a complete data-flow or SAST result; unresolved dependency calls in CcmParser were verified against source but their runtime semantics were not.
No unreported workspace code or transitive dependency source was reviewed, and no Jenkins security configuration or node placement was inspected.
The downstream visibility of entity-derived Metric values in the Jenkins UI is inferred only to a limited extent and remains unverified.

rejected_leads.lead: Stored XSS through attacker-controlled Metric unit, classification, or file values
rejected_leads.reason: These strings enter Bug annotations, but the actual HTML/Jelly rendering and escaping behavior live in analysis-core and are not present in this snapshot. No source sink demonstrating missing escaping was found.

rejected_leads.lead: Null or malformed classification/line-number values causing build failure
rejected_leads.reason: A crafted report can trigger NullPointerException or number conversion failures, but this is primarily denial of service within the attacker-influenced build and does not cross a clear privilege boundary by itself.
This is a functional/help mismatch that broadens which workspace files reach the XML parser; it is not independently a vulnerability and is included as reachability context for the XXE candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Path traversal through Metric.file or the configurable Ant pattern
rejected_leads.reason: The snapshot does not show a file read or other security-sensitive sink for these values; downstream analysis-core and FilesParser behavior is unavailable and was not assumed.
This is a functional copy/paste defect, not a security vulnerability in the reviewed source.

summary: Static review of all 51 repository-visible files found one strong lead: the CCM report parser feeds build-workspace XML into Apache Commons Digester without restricting external entities. CcmPublisher and CcmReporter both reach this parser for freestyle and Maven jobs. The issue is source-supported but not runtime-confirmed; transitive parser defaults and downstream rendering are unavailable.
